analysis.title: Cooler US jobs growth supports a Federal Reserve pause in October
key_insights: September nonfarm payrolls rose +29k versus the +90k consensus, with 60k of downward revisions to prior months.
The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, driven by a partial recovery in the participation rate (people returning to the workforce).
Wage growth was 3% y/y versus 3.1% prior, which ING reads as no inflation threat from the jobs market.
Dovish-leaning comments from NY Fed president John Williams and Vice Chair Philip Jefferson suggest no urgency to hike, so the Fed leadership is leaning toward an October hold.
A hot September CPI print (due 14 October) would be needed to make the October meeting interesting. ING's call is that December is the next Fed hike.

Manufacturing jobs rose for a fourth consecutive month, with 72,000 added cumulatively since the start of the year. Advanced manufacturing (pharma, transport and aerospace, computing and electronics) is strongest, consistent with strong sector surveys.
Construction jobs also increased, potentially tied to data centre activity.
Services were weaker: information (-10k), financial (-7k), professional business services (-9k) and government (-17k) all fell.
The economy is low hire, low fire, and the lack of opportunities has led to a large fall in labour participation. The labour force rose 485,000 last month, lifting participation to 61.8% from 61.6%.

Unemployed people and job vacancies are now of similar number, versus two vacancies per unemployed American in early 2022. This is depressing wage growth, and the low quits rate suggests further downside risk to the current 3% rate.
ING believes market pricing of 3-4 Fed rate hikes looks too aggressive.

sector_views.rationale: Fourth consecutive monthly rise in manufacturing jobs, with 72k added year to date and strong survey readings, led by advanced manufacturing.
Information, financial, professional business services and government employment all fell in September.

The consensus estimate that the print missed.

Labour force rose 485,000, which lifted the unemployment rate.
No inflation threat from the jobs market. The low quits rate points to further downside risk.

macro_indicators.interpretation: ING expects an October hold and sees market pricing of 3-4 hikes as too aggressive.
A hot print would be needed to put an October hike in play.

risk_factors: A hot September CPI print (due 14 October) could revive the chance of an October Fed hike.
A choppy participation rate can move the unemployment rate unpredictably from month to month.
vol_and_positioning: ING says market pricing of 3-4 Fed rate hikes looks too aggressive, which implies the rate market is positioned for more tightening than ING expects.

tension_points.bear_case: Weak payrolls, 3% wage growth and dovish comments from Williams and Jefferson point to an October hold. ING sees the 3-4 hike pricing as too aggressive.
